headline.headline: GAME 7 SUNDAY: PISTONS AND CAVALIERS MEET IN WINNER-TAKE-ALL SHOWDOWN
headline.deck: Detroit's Game 6 rout sets up a Cleveland showdown neither city will forget.
headline.body:
DETROIT — The Cleveland Cavaliers and Detroit Pistons will settle their Eastern Conference semifinal series the only way worth settling it: in a Game 7, winner take all, Sunday night. The Pistons made certain of it Saturday, rolling past Cleveland 115-94 in a game that was never close after the first quarter, handing the Cavaliers their most lopsided loss of the postseason and sending the series back to Cleveland with all the momentum swinging toward Detroit.

Cade Cunningham controlled the game from start to finish, distributing the ball with surgical precision while Detroit's defense suffocated Donovan Mitchell, who finished well below his playoff average. The Pistons shot 52 percent from the field and outrebounded the Cavaliers by double digits, a performance that looked less like a desperate elimination game and more like a team announcing itself as a legitimate Eastern Conference force. Detroit entered the postseason at 30-to-1 odds to win the championship; those numbers will shorten considerably depending on what happens Sunday.

The Cavaliers, who own a proud Game 7 history of their own, return home to Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse knowing they have not lost a winner-take-all game in that building since LeBron James left for Los Angeles. Mitchell will need to shake off Saturday's disappointment fast. Tip-off is Sunday evening, and one franchise's season ends on the hardwood before the night is through.

secondary.headline: SPURS STEAMROLL TIMBERWOLVES, PUSH SERIES TO COMMANDING POSITION
secondary.deck: San Antonio's 139-109 demolition leaves Minnesota reeling heading into elimination.
secondary.body:
MINNEAPOLIS — While the Pistons and Cavaliers grabbed the Eastern headlines Saturday, the Western Conference semifinal between the San Antonio Spurs and Minnesota Timberwolves delivered a message just as blunt. The Spurs dismantled Minnesota 139-109, a 30-point statement that exposed the Timberwolves' defensive breakdowns and turned what many expected to be a competitive series into something resembling a mismatch.

Victor Wembanyama was an absolute terror, altering shots at the rim while contributing across the box score in a display that reminded a national audience why San Antonio's rebuild accelerated so dramatically. Anthony Edwards fought hard for Minnesota but received little help from a supporting cast that wilted under the Spurs' pace and shooting efficiency. The Timberwolves now face the prospect of elimination, needing to solve a San Antonio team that appears to be peaking at precisely the right moment of the playoffs.

secondary.headline: MARTINEZ DELIVERS THE BLOW AS GUARDIANS RALLY PAST REDS
secondary.deck: Angel Martinez's seventh-inning homer caps Cleveland comeback; Ramirez makes franchise history.
secondary.body:
CLEVELAND — Angel Martinez stepped into the box in the seventh inning Saturday night with the Cincinnati Reds holding the lead and delivered a two-run home run that turned the game around and lifted the Cleveland Guardians to a 7-4 victory at Progressive Field. The go-ahead shot silenced a Reds lineup that had been scrapping all night and handed Cleveland a series split it desperately needed after struggling through a competitive weekend.

The bigger number, though, may belong to Jose Ramirez, who moved into sixth place on the Guardians' all-time franchise history list with his offensive contributions Saturday night. Ramirez has been the heartbeat of this Cleveland ballclub for nearly a decade, and milestones accumulate around him the way hits do. The Reds, who entered Saturday's game believing they had the weekend in hand, now regroup after letting a late lead slip away to one of the American League's most dangerous middle-of-the-order combinations.

secondary.headline: CANADIENS INCH TOWARD SECOND ROUND SERIES WIN AS SABRES FACE ELIMINATION
secondary.deck: Buffalo pulled goaltender Alex Lyon in Game 6 as Montreal tightened its series grip.
secondary.body:
BUFFALO — The Buffalo Sabres began Game 6 Saturday night with Alex Lyon in net and a franchise desperate to extend its second-round series against the Montreal Canadiens. They did not finish it that way. Lyon was pulled during the game as the Sabres chased the contest, and Montreal maintained enough of its structure and composure to keep Buffalo on the brink of elimination in a series the Canadiens have controlled with steady, suffocating defensive hockey.

Montreal's odds to advance have only improved as the series has progressed, and the Canadiens appear built for exactly this kind of grind-it-out playoff run. For Buffalo, the window to respond is now essentially shut unless the Sabres can produce something dramatic in what may be their final game of the season. The Carolina Hurricanes are already waiting in the wings, having watched this series closely as they prepare for a conference finals matchup against whichever team survives. Colorado, Carolina, and Vegas remain the Stanley Cup favorites, and Montreal's run has done nothing to change that calculus yet.

column.headline: GAME 7 IS THE GREATEST INVENTION IN SPORTS, AND SUNDAY PROVES IT
column.body:
No overtime period, no penalty shootout, no tiebreaker round robin has ever come close to matching what a Game 7 does to a city, a locker room, and a fan base. Sunday night, Cleveland and Detroit settle six games of basketball with one final forty-eight minutes, and the weight of that singular fact is almost too heavy to carry. The Cavaliers go home to their building. The Pistons carry their momentum. Somebody goes home for the summer before Monday morning arrives.

What makes this particular Game 7 extraordinary is the symmetry of the pressure. The Cavaliers have won Game 7s in that building before, and the memory of that history is both a comfort and a burden. The Pistons have spent years rebuilding toward exactly this kind of moment, and now that it has arrived, they have to prove Saturday night was not their ceiling. Cade Cunningham has never played in a Game 7 this consequential. Neither, essentially, has this version of the Detroit franchise. One of them finds out Sunday who they really are. That is the only kind of test that matters.

story.headline: MARLINS ERUPT FOR 8 IN THE 10TH, STUN RAYS AND SNAP 11-GAME SKID
story.deck: Liam Hicks delivers the key blow as Miami stages a stunning late-game comeback
story.body:
MIAMI — The Tampa Bay Rays thought they had seen enough from the Miami Marlins on Friday night, holding a comfortable lead heading into the tenth inning. Then the floodgates opened. Miami sent ten men to the plate, scored eight runs, and walked away with a 10-5 victory that snapped the Rays' 11-game winning streak in breathtaking fashion.

Liam Hicks provided the decisive blow, lacing a two-run RBI single into the outfield grass as the Marlins' bats refused to quit. The inning unfolded like a fever dream for Tampa Bay, as a bullpen that had been nearly untouchable during the winning streak suddenly could not find a single out without surrendering baserunners. By the time the Rays recorded the final outs, the damage was catastrophic and irreversible.

The loss snapped one of the more impressive streaks in the American League this season for Tampa Bay, which had ridden strong pitching and timely hitting through eleven consecutive wins. Miami, meanwhile, handed its long-suffering fanbase a night to remember, turning what looked like another quiet loss into a defining moment of the young season. The Marlins now carry genuine momentum into Sunday's rubber match.

story.headline: PISTONS POUND CAVALIERS, FORCE WINNER-TAKE-ALL GAME 7
story.deck: Detroit rolls Cleveland by 21 to set up Sunday showdown for Eastern Conference title
story.body:
CLEVELAND — The Detroit Pistons arrived at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse on Friday night and delivered a beating the Cavaliers will not soon forget, rolling to a 115-94 victory that forces a decisive Game 7 on Sunday and leaves Cleveland's Eastern Conference Finals dreams hanging by a thread.

Detroit controlled the game from the opening tip, never allowing Cleveland to find a rhythm on either end of the floor. The Pistons' defense suffocated the Cavaliers' perimeter shooters all night, and their offense moved with the kind of precision and urgency that defines teams playing their best basketball at the right moment. The 21-point margin was the largest of the series and sent a clear message that this Pistons squad intends to go the distance.

Now comes Sunday. Game 7. Both franchises carry proud histories in elimination games, but only one can advance to the NBA Finals. The Pistons enter as slight favorites despite playing on the road in 2024-25 — a remarkable position for a team that opened these playoffs at 30-1 odds to win the championship. For Cleveland, the question is whether the Cavaliers can summon something they could not find Friday night: an answer for Detroit's relentless defensive pressure.

story.headline: LYON PULLED AS SABRES FIGHT FOR SURVIVAL IN GAME 6 AGAINST CANADIENS
story.deck: Buffalo pulls its starter as Montreal closes in on a second-round berth.
story.body:
The Buffalo Sabres turned to Alex Lyon in a desperate attempt to extend their playoff lives Saturday night, then yanked him in Game 6 against the Montreal Canadiens with Buffalo facing elimination and the sellout crowd at KeyBank Center holding its breath. Lyon, who had carried the Sabres through stretches of a bruising first-round series, could not hold the fort as Montreal's relentless offense kept pouring pucks on net. The Canadiens, riding the momentum of a raucous home crowd and a healthy roster, entered the night one win away from punching their ticket to the second round.

The stakes could not be higher for a Buffalo franchise that has waited decades for a deep playoff run. The Sabres now face the prospect of watching Montreal advance to meet the Carolina Hurricanes, who have been idle and rested, awaiting the winner of this first-round series. Carolina remains one of the Stanley Cup favorites alongside the Colorado Avalanche and Vegas Golden Knights, according to the latest oddsmakers' lines, which peg the Hurricanes as a formidable obstacle for whichever team survives this bruising battle.

While the playoff drama unfolded in Buffalo, Canadian hockey fans had another reason to cheer Saturday. Macklin Celebrini, the consensus top prospect and face of the sport's future, scored twice and added an assist as Canada routed Italy 6-0 at the World Championships to improve to 2-0 in group play. Celebrini's performance offered a glimpse of the star power that could define the sport for a generation, even as the NHL's immediate focus remained fixed on who would shake hands first in the Sabres-Canadiens series.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 CAMPAIGN
story.deck: Several franchises make bold moves at the game's most important position this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has produced a flurry of quarterback movement unlike anything seen in recent memory, with multiple franchises overhauling their most critical position in the weeks following Super Bowl LX. The Cleveland Browns, desperate to end years of instability under center, agreed to terms with veteran signal-caller Sam Darnold on a three-year deal worth $112 million, betting that his late-career resurgence can finally bring respectability to a long-suffering franchise. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders swung a blockbuster trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, acquiring Russell Wilson in exchange for two first-round picks and a pair of young defensive starters.

The New England Patriots continued their methodical rebuild under head coach Jerod Mayo, selecting Tennessee quarterback Nico Iamaleava with the fifth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft held last month in Green Bay. The pick drew praise from league personnel evaluators who regard Iamaleava as the most pro-ready passer in a deep draft class. The Patriots also added veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs on a restructured one-year prove-it deal, giving their new franchise quarterback an experienced target to lean on during what figures to be a transitional season in Foxborough.

With training camps scheduled to open in late July, several other storylines are heating up across the league. The Dallas Cowboys released four-time Pro Bowl receiver CeeDee Lamb after contract negotiations collapsed for the second consecutive offseason, sending shockwaves through the NFC and immediately drawing interest from the San Francisco 49ers and Detroit Lions. The defending Super Bowl LX champion Philadelphia Eagles, meanwhile, are focused on retaining linebacker Nakobe Dean, whose market has exploded after a dominant postseason run that culminated in the franchise's second championship in eight years.
